title: The Clark Kent Calzone
headnote: This was the very first dish I made in the food truck. Luca Castiglione, who owned the truck previously and from whom we bought it, was my guide to this recipe, which he used to sell from the truck - which was previously called Limoncello. I put my own spin on the filling for the calzone, by making a Biltong and Brinjal filling!

groups.heading: For the calzone dough
ingredients: 2 tsp dry yeast (or mix active yeast with water)
steps: Mix all the ingredients together and knead the dough thoroughly.
Place the dough in a greased bowl and cover with a damp cloth. Let it rise for 1 hour.
Roll out the risen dough and form small balls. Place the balls on a baking tray and allow to rise for another hour.

groups.heading: For the Free State Calzone filling
steps: Combine the ingredients for your chosen filling and mix well.

groups.heading: For the Tomato Sauce
ingredients: A generous drizzle of olive oil
steps: Mix all the ingredients together and set aside.

groups.heading: For the Calzone
steps: Preheat the oven to 240°C.
Roll out a dough ball and place a handful of filling in the center.
Fold the dough over the filling, seal the edges, and cut into a half-moon shape.
Place on a greased baking tray and drizzle a small amount of tomato sauce over the top.
Bake for 10 minutes or until golden brown.

caption: Our god children: Lua and Steph van der merwe

title: The Joker Hotdog
headnote: Arnold Tanzer is like a mentor to me. Arnold was the culinary producer on MasterChef and we became fast friends and still are to this day. For the second episode of the series, Arnold was working as the catering company for a production of the BBC series in Cape Town. We set up the food truck to feed the crew and made my favourite dish in the world… hotdogs! This Sriracha and Honey Glazed Frankfurter Hotdogs with Mayonnaise Coleslaw is amazing… And we make our own Mayo!

groups.heading: For the Coleslaw
ingredients: ½ head of cabbage, finely shredded
steps: In a large bowl, combine the cabbage and grated carrots. Stir in the mayonnaise until evenly coated.
Mix the honey and sriracha sauce. Brush the mixture over the frankfurters and grill or fry until caramelised.
Place each glazed frankfurter into hotdog roll. Add a generous serving of coleslaw on top.

groups.heading: For the Mayonnaise (approx. 250 ml)
steps: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature. Lightly whisk the egg yolks, then add salt and pepper to taste.
Add the mustard and lemon juice, whisking until combined.
Slowly add the olive oil in small amounts while whisking continuously until the mayonnaise is thick and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

title: Taco Whiz
headnote: As part of the cooking show, I cooked with some of my food heroes in and around the Western Cape. My friend, Chef Henry Vigar, shared this Tuna Tacos with burnt corn, chimichuri & smoked aubergine puree recipe in the show and now I’m sharing it with you!

groups.heading: For the taco dough
steps: Burn the onions until black, processed to a powder in the food processor.
Add all the ingredients in a food processor and mix until a dough forms. Remove and let rest for 15 minutes under a wet cloth.
Make palm size balls and roll out very thin. In a dry pan, fry for about two minutes on each side and keep aside.

groups.heading: For the eggplant puree
ingredients: 3 cloves of garlic, chopped and pan-fried
steps: Burn the eggplant over an open flame. You can also do it on the grill. Remove the peel.
Add the pan-fried onions and garlic to the aubergine in a food processor and blend. Keep aside.

groups.heading: For the Tuna
steps: Fry tuna on both sides for about one minute.
Mix together the ingredients for the marinade. Slice the tuna. Let the tuna rest in the marinade until serving.

groups.heading: For the chimichurri
steps: Blend all the ingredients in a food processor until fine.

groups.heading: For the extras
ingredients: 300g assorted small tomatoes, sliced and marinated in a basil and olive oil mixture
2 corns, boiled and fried and de-stalked

groups.heading: How do you put it all together?
steps: Layer in this order: tacos, eggplant puree, tomatoes, lettuce, onions, tuna, corn, onion ash, and finish with coriander & chimichurri.

caption: KAPOW @ ROBERTSON Voorbereidingskool

title: Butter Chicken
headnote: One of my favourite humans I met on MasterChef was the season 1 runner-up, Sue-Ann Allen. We cooked together in the Bo-Kaap and made Butter Chicken Rotti’s as part of Padkos. It was a fun shoot and this Butter Chicken recipe is a staple in our house.

groups.heading: For the Butter chicken
steps: Combine the chicken, garam masala, tandoori masala, cumin powder, salt, yogurt, and oil. Marinate for a few hours (or overnight).
Fry the marinated chicken in a non-stick pan with the oil until almost cooked. Remove from heat and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the cooking oil and sauté the onion until soft and translucent. Add the paprika, garlic, and ginger, cooking gently until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato pasata and simmer for about 20 minutes, until the oil begins to separate from the sauce.

Add the chicken pieces back to the sauce along with the butter and cream. Cook for a few minutes until heated through. Stir in the fresh coriander and increase the heat until the sauce just begins to bubble.

title: The Vixen Burger
headnote: As part of the cooking show, I cooked with some of my food heroes in and around the Western Cape. This is my friend and colleague/judge from MasterChef South Africa, Chef Pete Goffe-Wood’s Burger Patty recipe. It is Incredible! And the sweet mustard sauce is my late aunt Zannie’s. Its delectable!

groups.heading: For the Burger Patties
steps: Mince the chuck and brisket together.
Add the eggs to the mince and mix well. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
On a lightly oiled surface, take a handful of mince, roll it into a ball, and flatten it. Use a mold to shape the patties if desired.
Place the patties on wax paper on a baking tray and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes. Patties can also be frozen for later use.

groups.heading: For the sweet mustard sauce
steps: Whisk all the ingredients for Zannie’s Sweet Mustard (page 48) together until smooth.
Cook in a double boiler (or use a glass bowl over a pot of boiling water) for 20-30 minutes until the mixture thickens. Stir occasionally.
Store in the refrigerator once cooled.

groups.heading: For the Burgers
steps: Toast the burger buns lightly.
Assemble the burger by layering lettuce, tomato slices, a cooked patty, a slice of smoked provolone cheese, and Zannie’s sweet mustard sauce (Recipe on page 48) on the bun.

title: Poke-Mon
headnote: Suzie Holtzhausen is a super-chef… especially with seafood. Her and I had the best fun making this very South African take on a Poke bowl - A Hawaiian Tuna Ceviche, with Biltong Dust and Naartjie, served with Spanspek & Deep-fried Seaweed.

groups.heading: For the Tuna Poké
ingredients: 1 kg fresh tuna, diced into 1 cm cubes
1 thumb-sized piece of fresh ginger, finely chopped
1 bunch of spring onions, finely chopped

groups.heading: For Serving
ingredients: A small bowl of seaweed, fried for 10 seconds
steps: Combine all the ingredients, except for the citrus juices (naartjie, lime, and lemon juice), in a large mixing bowl. Let the mixture sit for a few minutes.
Add the citrus juices to the mixture and stir well to combine.
Serve: Place 2-3 slices of cantaloupe on top of each serving of Tuna Poké. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and fried seaweed.

title: Killer Croquettes
time: Prep 20 min (plus cooling) | Cook 15 min | Chill overnight
headnote: My path crossed with Chef Matt Manning in 2013 when I went to a OneIngredient Dinner with Sue-Anne Allen & Ilse Nel, two Masterchef contestants who I would later work with again. Matt’s One Ingredient for that dinner was Apricot. He infused a five course menu, of which we had to cook our own starts and mains, with Apricot. Later one we became good friends and Matt filmed with me for Padkos - We made these killer Mac & Cheese croquettes… and its insane! Golden, crispy, cheesy bites — perfect as a snack, starter or party treat

groups.heading: For the Mac ’n Cheese
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Boil the macaroni in salted water until al dente. Drain and set aside.
In a bowl, whisk together the cream, milk, and 3 eggs. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine the cooked pasta with the cream mixture and grated Parmesan. Stir to coat evenly. Pour the pasta mixture into a baking tray and spread evenly.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until completely firm — ideally overnight.
Once firm, cut the set macaroni mixture into cubes. Dredge each cube first in flour, then dip in the beaten egg, and coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pot or fryer to 180°C. Fry the croquettes in batches until golden brown. Remove and drain on paper towels. Serve immediately.

title: The Spider-Man Vetkoek
headnote: I had the pleasure to cook with the late and great Lentswe Benghu, as well as going to Langa in Cape Town to try Umqombothi and Skaapkop. I’ve had skaapkop on the farm before, but the experience was amazing. In the vain of the offal, we then preceded to make Magwinya (Vetkoek) with a Peri Peri Chicken liver. It was a magical day.

groups.heading: For the Vetkoek
ingredients: Oil for greasing and frying (deep or shallow)
steps: On a flat surface, mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Gradually add the lukewarm water to form a manageable dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes. Lightly grease the dough with oil, cover, and let it rise in a warm place until doubled in size (about 2 hours).

Gently punch down the dough and roll it into a long roll, approximately 4 cm in diameter. Pinch off pieces about 4 cm in size and flatten them to 1 cm thick. Let them rise slightly on a greased surface.
Heat oil in a large pan or pot for deep or shallow frying, as preferred. Fry the vetkoek until golden brown on both sides. Drain on paper towels.

groups.heading: For Peri-Peri Chicken Liver Filling
ingredients: 250 g chicken livers, rinsed in water
10 red chilies, deseeded and finely chopped
steps: Sauté the onion, chilies, and red peppers over medium heat for 10-15 minutes until softened. Deglaze the pan with red wine vinegar.
Add the smoked paprika and let the mixture simmer for 20 minutes. Blend in a food processor until smooth.
Mix the peri-peri sauce with the raw chicken livers and let it marinate for a few minutes.
Heat a pan with olive oil and fry the chicken livers. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice open the vetkoek and fill with the peri-peri chicken livers. Serve warm and enjoy!

title: West Coast Mussels
headnote: Kobus van der Merwe from Wolfgat in Paternoster was one of my favourite guests in the Food truck. Kobus is generous of spirit and kind at heart. We foraged for mussels and seaweed and made West coast mussels in a beurre blanc sauce, as well as ‘hoenderboudjie’ - Kobus’ very clever bread sticks to mop up all the deliciousness. Enjoy this elegant West Coast dish — fresh, briny, and beautifully balanced.

groups.heading: For the Mussels
ingredients: 1 kg fresh West Coast mussels, in shell
A generous glug of olive oil
100 g sea coral (or julienned celery as substitute)
100 g sea lettuce (or pea shoots as substitute)
100 g pickled beach greens (or cos lettuce leaves as substitute)

groups.heading: For the Hoenderboudjie breadsticks
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roll the dough into a 10 cm log, then thin out the ends to resemble a chicken drumstick (“hoenderbeentjie”). Sprinkle with sea salt and dried herbs. Bake for 12 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. Set aside.
In a large pot, heat a good glug of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the mussels, cover with a lid and steam until they begin to open and go quiet.
Lift the lid and pour in the glass of Sauvignon Blanc. Cover again and steam for 2 minutes, just enough to cook off the alcohol. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve and set aside.
Allow the mussels to cool slightly, then remove from the shells. Return the mussels to the cooking liquid and warm through.
Remove the mussels again, add a generous splash of cream to the liquid, stir, and heat gently. Set aside the creamy sauce.
On each plate, arrange 5–6 mussels per portion. Add a few Cape gooseberries, sea coral (or celery), sea lettuce (or pea shoots), and pickled greens (or cos leaves).
Spoon over a little of the creamy wine sauce. Serve immediately with warm hoenderbeentjiebroodjies on the side.

title: Prawn, Avo & Mango Salad
headnote: This summer dish featured in the second season of Padkos, and is a light, tropical salad packed with sweet mango, creamy avocado, and a zesty citrus dressing.

ingredients: 2 mangos, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
2 limes, plus extra lime wedges for serving
⅓ cup coriander leaves, finely chopped
1 long red chilli, seeds removed and finely chopped
1 tbsp avocado oil or extra virgin olive oil
steps: Peel and devein the prawns. Roughly chop half of them and leave the rest whole for garnish. In a large bowl, combine the chopped prawns, mango cubes, and avocado.
Grate the zest of half a lime and juice both limes. In a small bowl, whisk together the lime zest and juice, coriander, chilli, honey, and oil. Season well with salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the prawn mixture and toss gently to combine.

Divide the butter lettuce leaves among serving plates and spoon the salad into each. Top with the remaining whole prawns, lime wedges, and micro herbs (if using). Serve immediately for a refreshing starter or light main.

tips: This salad pairs beautifully with a chilled glass of Sauvignon Blanc or a crisp rosé.

title: Chef Henry’s Cheesy Truffles
time: Prep 30 min | Chill overnight | Cook 10 min
headnote: Chef Henry Vigar shared this great recipe with me. I had my 40th birthday at his restaurant La Mouette in 2015. Perfect as a canapé, snack, or indulgent starter!

groups.heading: For the truffle balls
ingredients: 100 g grated Fontina cheese (or similar melting cheese)

groups.heading: For coating and frying
steps: Bring the milk to a simmer in a saucepan. In another large saucepan, melt the butter, then add the cake flour and cornflour. Stir constantly and cook out for 1 minute without letting it colour.
Gradually add the hot milk, whisking continuously. Bring to the boil and cook for 5 minutes, until the mixture thickens and starts to pull away from the sides of the pan.
Remove from the heat and whisk in the grated Fontina cheese. Add a drizzle of truffle oil and season with salt to taste. Cover and refrigerate overnight until firm.
Once chilled and set, roll the mixture into small balls (about the size of a walnut). Coat each ball by rolling it in semolina or flour, then dip in beaten egg, and coat in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to high temperature (about 180°C) and fry the balls until golden and crisp. Optional: give them a few seconds in a hot oven to finish heating through, if needed.
Serve hot with a sprinkle of salt, or with a dipping sauce of your choice. Goes really well with Zannie’s Sweet Mustard Sauce (Page 48).

title: Bertus Basson’s Caeser Salad
headnote: Bertus Basson is one of South Africa’s best chefs. He is also a stand-up human and takes direction very well. I should know. We filmed 3 seasons of Bertus’ show ‘Goed Beter Bertus’ for via, where we followed his day to day life with his multiple restaurants and his family life. But Bertus always made time to feed the crew. This easy Caesar Salad was whipped up one day for a quick lunch. if you want to you can joosh it up with some fried bacon bits or even some chicken breasts…

steps: Use the side of a chef’s knife to paste the garlic and anchovies together.
Mix the Worcestershire and mustard sauces in a bowl. Add the lemon juice, parmesan, black pepper and garlic/anchovy paste and combine with a whisk.
Whilst whisking, add the oils slowly to emulsify the mixture.
Once emulsified, ad the cos lettuce and mix to cover the leaves well. Add the croutons & extra parmesan and serve.

tips: If you have fresh tuna, you can add seared tuna to this dish…

title: Moroccan Roast Carrot and Avocado Salad
headnote: This is a delicious side dish to any winter stew, and is a real winner at dinner. Enjoy this vibrant, warm salad full of bold Moroccan flavours! We filmed this dish as part of Ilse Kook!, a cooking show on kykNET.

groups.heading: For the Salad
ingredients: 500 g mixed-colour medium carrots (with leafy tops if available)
Approx. 60 ml extra olive oil and vinegar (for dressing)
200 g mixed winter leaves (e.g., rocket, radicchio, witlof)
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Parboil the carrots in salted boiling water for 10 minutes, until nearly tender. Drain and transfer to a roasting tray.
In a pestle and mortar, grind the cumin seeds, dried chillies, sea salt, and black pepper. Add garlic, thyme leaves, olive oil, and vinegar. Pound into a paste.
Pour the paste over the carrots and toss to coat. Add the orange and lemon halves, cut-side down, to the tray. Roast in the oven for 25–30 minutes, or until golden.
Halve, peel, and stone the avocados. Cut into wedges lengthwise and place in a large bowl. Add the roasted carrots and torn ciabatta to the bowl with the avocados.
Squeeze the juice from the roasted orange and lemon into a bowl. Add any pan juices. Mix with equal parts olive oil and a splash of vinegar. Season to taste.
Toss the roasted vegetables, avocado, ciabatta, mixed leaves, and cress with the dressing. Arrange on a serving platter or divide between plates.
Top with a dollop of yoghurt and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

title: Tomato and Pancetta Braai Chicken with Olives
headnote: Another recipe from Ilse Kook. A hearty, flavour-packed dish perfect for a family feast or festive table!. This is a go to in our house, and the left-overs the next day is incredible… if there are left-overs.

ingredients: 1 red onion, cut into thin wedges
¼ cup fresh basil and oregano (plus extra for serving)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in an ovenproof roasting dish. Brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same dish, sauté the onion gently until soft. Add the chilli flakes and stir through. Place half of the sliced tomatoes and half of the cherry tomatoes over the sautéed onions.

Spread evenly, then return the chicken pieces to the dish, placing them on top of the tomatoes. Scatter the remaining tomatoes, basil, oregano, and thyme over the chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Drizzle over the wine and the remaining olive oil. Tuck the halved garlic bulb among the chicken pieces.
Roast uncovered for 1 to 1½ hours, until the chicken is golden brown and the tomato mixture is rich and jammy. Add the olives to the dish.

Lay the pancetta slices on top of the chicken and grill under the oven’s broiler for 4–5 minutes, or until crispy. Crumble the crisped pancetta over the dish and scatter with the remaining fresh herbs before serving.

title: Gregg Hammond’s 24 Hour Herb Crusted Beef Fillet
headnote: Working on the first season of the hit BBC show, Come Dine With Me South Africa was an experience to say the least! This fantastic Beef Fillet Recipe is from one of that season’s episodes, where the winner of the episode - a Men’s Health Model called Gregg Hammond - made this incredible dish!

ingredients: 1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, roughly chopped
steps: Remove any sinewy parts of the fillet. Place the fillet in a container where it fits snugly. Add the balsamic vinegar and coat the fillet throroughtly. Close the container and place in the fridge for 6 hour (or overnight).
Preheat oven to 200°C. Remove the fillet from the balsamic vinegar and pat dry with kitchen towel.
Add all the herbs in a casserole. Roll the fillet in the herbs. Place the fillet in a baking dish and in the oven for 15 minutes.

title: Heirloom Tomato and Whipped Feta Tart
headnote: This delicious tart is easy to make and super-tasty, This recipe is an adaptation to one of the tarts we filmed for the Plaaskombuis series, which I adapted a little.

steps: Preheat oven to 210°C. Line a 26cm square roaster with pastry, folding the edges over slightly.
Combine lemon zest with whipped feta, spread onto the pastry base, and scatter the tomatoes on top.
Brush edges of pastry with milk, fold over, and brush again. Bake for 20–30 minutes until golden brown.
Allow to cool slightly, garnish with chives, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper.

title: Andrea Burgner’s Cilbir
headnote: Having met and worked with Andrea Burgner, owner of The Leopard in Johannesburg, was one of the coolest experiences of my food journey. Andrea started out as a home cook with a knack for great combo’s. This Turkish Style breakfast is a go-to-favourite.

ingredients: 2½ cups plain Greek-style yoghurt (or use the labneh recipe from page 46)
A few fresh or dried sage
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Stir the garlic into the yoghurt (or labneh) and spread evenly over two serving plates to form little beds for the eggs.

Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil, add the vinegar, and gently lower the first egg into the water. (Creating a whirlpool is optional, though not essential.) Poach each egg for about 3 minutes for a soft yolk. Keep the poached eggs warm under a lid or on a warm plate.
While the eggs are cooking, melt the butter in a pan. Stir in the sage (if using fresh, fry until crisp) or parsley. Add the paprika and remove from the heat.

Remove the eggs with a slotted spoon and place them gently onto the yoghurt. Spoon the paprika butter over the eggs, season with sea salt and black pepper, and serve immediately with lots of warm bread.

tips: Oil a piece of clingwrap in a cup, add the egg and tie up. Poach in the plastic and remove he egg when cooked.

title: Easy Milktart
headnote: In the show Plaaskombuis, I had the distinct pleasure to travel with Elma Postma and a small team and direct the show. The premise was that we would go to farm kitchen’s across South Africa and cook with the men and woman of the farming community in their kitchens. This recipe is from Owen & Louise McGregor, from the farm Bagdad’s Cafe where they serve this easy milktart in the farm stall.

groups.heading: For the Crust
steps: Grease a medium-sized tart dish. Crush the Tennis biscuits finely and mix them with the melted butter or margarine.
Press the mixture firmly into the prepared tart dish, using the back of a spoon to push the crumbs against the bottom and sides. Refrigerate until needed.

groups.heading: For the Filling
steps: Heat 750 ml (3 cups) of the milk with the vanilla and almond essence in a saucepan over medium heat until just below boiling point. Add the butter or margarine and allow it to melt in the milk.
In a separate bowl, mix the sugar, cornstarch, and custard powder with the remaining 250 ml (1 cup) of milk. Add the eggs and whisk well.
Slowly add a little of the warm milk mixture to the egg mixture, whisking continuously to temper the eggs. Pour the tempered egg mixture in a thin stream back into the saucepan, stirring constantly.
Continue stirring over medium heat until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil.
Pour the filling into the prepared crust and smooth it out evenly. Lightly sprinkle ground cinnamon over the top and allow the tart to cool to room temperature before serving.

title: Broccoli Chicken Bake
headnote: My mom, Marikie, used to make this for us as kids, and to this day, it's one of my favourites. You’ll need a whole rotisserie chicken for this one…

ingredients: 1 can (425 g) cream of mushroom soup
1 cooked chicken, deboned and cut into pieces
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Boil the broccoli for 10 minutes until tender but not mushy. Drain well and set aside.
Mix the cream of mushroom soup, curry powder, and mayonnaise in a bowl. Set aside.
Grease a baking dish. Layer the cooked broccoli and chicken in the dish. Pour the mayonnaise mixture evenly over the layers.
Mix the melted butter with the breadcrumbs and grated parmesan cheese. Sprinkle over the dish. Place in the preheated oven and bake for about 30 minutes, until golden brown on top.
Best served with noodles and a fresh salad.

title: Handrie’s Tamatiebredie
headnote: Of all the food that my darling husband makes, this dish is probably one of my favourite. He would start very early in the morning and really take his time to get this dish just right. Here is an approximation of Tamatiebredie - a perfect comfort dish for winter days.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb stewing meat or lamb shanks (skenkels), cut into chunks
1 tbsp ground allspice (with flour for meat)
A good chug of Worsthershire sauce
2 x 400 g tin chopped tomatoes (or 6 ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped)
1 tsp sugar (to balance the acidity of the tomatoes)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Fresh coriander or parsley, to garnish
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Coat the lamb in flour and allspice mix. Add the lamb pieces to the pot and brown them well on all sides. Remove and set aside.

In the same pot, reduce the heat and sauté the onions until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and cook for another minute. Stir in the coriander and paprika. Cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste, bay leaves, worchesstershire sauce and water. Then add the browned meat, bring to the boil, then reduce to simmer for 1 hour.
After the hour, add the chopped tomatoes & sugar, stir well and season with salt and pepper. Cover the pot and let it simmer gently for about 1½ hours, or until the lamb is tender.
Add the potatoes in the last 30–40 minutes of cooking, stirring occasionally. Add more water if needed to prevent sticking.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with chopped fresh coriander or parsley. Serve with fluffy white rice, pap, or crusty bread to soak up the rich tomato gravy.

title: Tata’s Khuku
headnote: This recipe is from my good friend Arnold Tanzer. He made this tasty chicken dish and we filmed it as part of a Mandela Day celebration. The late president Nelson Mandela’s favourite dish…

ingredients: 4 chicken drumsticks & 4 thighs, or whole chicken cut in 8 pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Place cut red onions in a roasting tray, and add the chicken on top.
In a separate bowl, mix chutney and fresh ginger. add the chilli flakes, paprika, curry, cumin and coriander and combine. Pour in the chicken stock and whisk until incorporated.
Pour the sauce over the chicken pieces and coat the chicken pieces. Cook skin-up for 20 minutes, then turn every so often.
After an hour, season with salt and pepper, and serve on your favourite starch with lemon wedges.

title: Orzo & Chicken Bake
headnote: This bake is really delicious and easy to make

steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Place the onions, peppers, garlic and rosa tomatoes in a rectangular bowl, cover in olive oil and salt and pepper. Roast for 25 minutes.
Add the orzo over the roasted veggies and add the creme fraiche in the middle. add stock over and bake for 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven and mix through. Add the chicken thighs, and place back in the oven for 25 minutes.
Remove and add the grated cheese and season to taste.

tips: Serve with a chilled Pinot Noir.

title: Beef Lasagne
headnote: Our good friend and colleague Darren Lindsay and his wonderful wife Ashleigh, have two boys - Charlie & Ollie - and this recipe is their favourite.

groups.heading: For the Meat Sauce (Ragù)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pan. Sauté the onion, garlic, carrots, and celery until softened. Add the beef mince and brown well.
Stir in tomato paste, tinned tomatoes, red wine (if using), oregano, salt, pepper, and sugar. Simmer on low for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add a splash of water if it becomes too thick.

groups.heading: For the Béchamel Sauce
steps: In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually add warm milk while whisking to avoid lumps. Simmer until the sauce thickens. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.

groups.heading: To assemble
ingredients: Olive oil or butter, for greasing
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a large baking dish. Spread a thin layer of meat sauce on the base.
Add a layer of lasagne sheets, followed by meat sauce, then béchamel. Repeat the layers, finishing with béchamel. Top with grated mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover loosely with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Mother-in-Law - Anita’s Mac n Cheese
headnote: I know there is another Mac and Cheese recipe in the book already, BUT nobody can beat my mother-in-law, Anita Basson’s Mac & Cheese. She is quite particular about certain things that need to go into the dish, and I have not gotten it like she makes it… yet… but this is A version of Anita’s Mac N Cheese. And I checked it with her…

ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Cook the pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over low heat. Add the flour and whisk until the butter absorbs the flour completely.
Pour in all the milk at once and whisk to combine thoroughly. Continue whisking over low heat for 5–10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the flour is cooked through.
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the grated cheddar cheese. Once the cheese is melted, mix the drained macaroni into the cheese sauce.
Layer the dish in the following order: Cheese, Macaroni, Tomato. Do this twice ending with a layer of cheese. Sprinkle the top with grated Parmesan. Bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown on top.
Enjoy hot from the oven with a crisp green salad or roasted veggies on the side.

title: Easy Focaccia
headnote: A good focaccia will elevate any meal into a feast. This recipe works best if you give the dough time to settle… so make the dough and do the initial proving 2 days before you bake the focaccia.

steps: Add all the ingredients in a bowl and mix until combined with a wooden spoon. Cover and rest in a warm place for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and stretch and pull the mixture. Cover and let prove for 30 minutes.
Using olive oil on your hands, do another stretch and pull. With the soft side up, cover in olive oil, then cling-wrap and place in fridge overnight (or even over 2 nights).
Line the baking tray with baking paper and olive oil. Add the dough, cover up and prove for 2 hours.
Olive oil on the hands, get your fingers into the dough to dimple it. Add olives and rosemary twigs (covered in oil) - or your topping of choice - and bake at 200 C for 18-22 minutes.
Serve immediately with good Balsamic Vinegar and Olive oil.

title: Whole Roasted Cauliflower with Cheesy Béchamel
headnote: A show-stopping vegetarian dish — tender roasted cauliflower smothered in a rich, cheesy sauce and baked to golden perfection.

groups.heading: For the Cauliflower
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place the whole cauliflower in a large pot of boiling salted water. Simmer for 10–12 minutes until just tender. Drain well and let sit for a few minutes to dry out.
Place the cauliflower in a lightly greased ovenproof dish. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast uncovered for 20–25 minutes until golden in places.

groups.heading: For the Béchamel Sauce
steps: In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes to form a roux.
Gradually add the warm milk, whisking continuously to avoid lumps. Simmer for 5–6 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the mustard, grated cheddar, and season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste. Once the cheese is melted and the sauce is smooth, remove from heat.

Pour the béchamel generously over the roasted cauliflower, covering it completely. Top with an extra handful of grated cheese (optional). Return to the oven and bake for 20–25 minutes, or until the top is golden and bubbling.

groups.heading: To Serve
steps: Serve hot as a vegetarian centrepiece with crusty bread or as a decadent side dish to roasts or grilled meats. Garnish with chopped parsley or chives for extra colour and freshness.

title: Cannellini Beans with Roast Tomatoes & Basil
headnote: This is a favourite in our house, where my husband, Handrie, makes this delicious vegetarian dish. Best enjoyed with crusty toasted sourdough.

ingredients: 250 g tomatoes (halve or chop if large; leave cherry tomatoes whole)
1 x 400 g tin cannellini beans, drained
1 tbsp Creme fraiche or cream cheese
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Place the tomatoes in a baking tray along with the thyme sprigs, whole garlic clove, a generous drizzle of olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Roast at 190°C (fan) for 20–25 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft and blistered.
Remove the tray from the oven, squash the roasted garlic clove with a fork and stir it into the tomatoes.
Add the cannellini beans, stir gently, and return to the oven for 5–10 minutes to warm through.
Remove thyme stalks. Stir in the mascarpone and fresh basil leaves. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Drizzle with a little more olive oil and enjoy with warm, crusty bread.

title: Ham & Cheese Croissant Croque Monsieur
headnote: An easy breakfast meal, this one can be made and put in the fridge overnight and then popped into the oven the next morning before serving it. It is super easy to make and a lovely treat.

steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C. In a large bowl, whisk together the milk, eggs, minced garlic, mustard powder, salt, black pepper, thyme and cayenne pepper until thoroughly combined.
Cut each croissant in half lengthwise, as if opening it for a sandwich. Then, slice each half into 4 smaller pieces.

Lightly grease a 25 cm ovenproof skillet or a 2-litre baking dish. Place half of the croissant pieces along the bottom of the dish. Layer with chopped ham, half of the shredded Swiss and white cheddar cheeses. Add the remaining croissant pieces on top, tearing them into smaller pieces if necessary to create a snug layer.

Evenly pour the egg mixture over the croissants. Gently press the top layer of croissants into the mixture, ensuring they are soaked. Let the casserole rest for 20 minutes, or until the bread has fully absorbed the liquid. (For convenience, you can refrigerate the casserole overnight, keeping it covered.)
After resting, sprinkle the remaining shredded cheese evenly over the top. Bake the casserole uncovered for 40–45 minutes, or until puffed and golden.
Allow the casserole to cool slightly—it will deflate as it cools. Serve warm and enjoy!

title: Biltong Soup
headnote: This recipe is a family favourite and one that gives me oodles of nostalgia. Very rich and damn delicious! I loved it as a kid, but later on realised it's a thinned version of Roux, which is what makes it so rich!

ingredients: 80 g finely grated biltong + thin slices for garnish
freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat and sauté the garlic for a few seconds. Stir in the flour, nutmeg, coriander, and black pepper until well combined.
Gradually add the milk, stock, and cream, stirring continuously to prevent lumps. Let the soup simmer, stirring occasionally. Add more milk if a thinner consistency is desired.
Add the grated biltong and cheeses, stirring until melted and well incorporated. Just before serving, stir in the sherry.
Garnish each bowl with thin slices of biltong and serve with fresh, warm bread.

title: JH’s Clear Chicken Soup with Herb Dumplings
headnote: This is a recipe from one of my food heroes, Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen. We ate at his Michelin-star restaurant, Jan, in Nice in 2017. He is also as charming as he is talented.

groups.heading: For the Chicken Soup
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, on the bone with the skin on
1 onion, peeled and cut into chunks
1 celery stalk, cut into chunks (including the leaves)
1 leek, rinsed and cut into chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat some olive oil in a large saucepan. Add the chicken breasts and fry until lightly browned. Add all the remaining soup ingredients.
Cover with a lid and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer gently for at least 3 hours. Season with salt and pepper halfway through the cooking time.
Remove the chicken breasts, discard the skin and bones, shred the meat, and return it to the soup.

groups.heading: For the Herb Dumplings
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Rub in the butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in the chives, then gradually add the milk until a dough forms. You should be able to roll small balls. If the dough is too dry, add a touch more milk.
Roll the dough into small balls — they will expand as they cook.

Pour about 300 ml of the hot chicken soup into a large saucepan. Drop the dumplings in, cover with a lid, and simmer for 5 minutes. Turn the dumplings and cook uncovered for a further 5 minutes, until cooked through.

groups.heading: To Serve
steps: Spoon the hot chicken soup into serving bowls. Drop in a few dumplings per bowl. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

title: Gazpacho
headnote: This delicious cold soup is easy to make and super-delicious, It also reminds me of one of my favourite cocktails - the Bloody Mary (Recipe on Page 75).

ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
350g mixed red, yellow, and green tomatoes, halved (for garnish)
steps: Bring a large casserole of water to a boil, make an “X” incision on the tomato bottoms, and blanch for 15 seconds. Transfer tomatoes to an ice bath, peel, core, and seed them.
Blend tomatoes, onion, garlic, peppers, cucumber, and basil in a food processor until smooth.
Add tomato juice and vinegar, season, and chill overnight.
Garnish with halved tomatoes and fresh basil before serving.

title: Homemade Labneh
headnote: A thick, creamy Middle Eastern strained yoghurt cheese — tangy, versatile, and delicious as a dip or spread

steps: In a bowl, stir the salt, chilli and black pepper into the yoghurt until fully combined.
Line a fine mesh sieve with cheesecloth, muslin, or a clean kitchen towel and place over a bowl. Spoon the yoghurt into the cloth, gather the edges, and twist gently to enclose.
Place in the refrigerator and allow to drain for 12–24 hours, depending on how thick you want your labneh.
After 12 hours, the labneh will be soft and spreadable (like cream cheese). For a firmer, tangier version, continue draining up to 24 hours.

Transfer the labneh to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 1 week. To serve, drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with za’atar, and add fresh herbs or nuts. Serve with warm pita, crackers, or crudités.

tips: To make labneh balls, roll the thickened labneh into small balls and store in a jar filled with olive oil and herbs — great for mezze platters! Also great to use in the Cilbir recipe on page 29.

title: Seven Layer Salad
headnote: A make-ahead classic — crisp lettuce, peas, bacon, and eggs layered with a tangy, creamy dressing

groups.heading: For the dressing
ingredients: 500 ml mayonnaise (or half mayonnaise, half plain yoghurt)
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, sugar, sour cream, and mustard until smooth. Adjust sweetness to taste.

groups.heading: For the salad
ingredients: 1 large head iceberg lettuce, coarsely shredded
1 large onion or red onion, halved and thinly sliced
1 green bell pepper, deseeded and sliced
2 packs streaky bacon (200–250 g each), diced and fried until crispy
4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and thickly sliced
steps: In a large glass salad bowl with straight sides, layer half of each salad ingredient in the following order: lettuce, onion, green pepper, peas, bacon, egg slices, grated cheese.
Spoon half of the dressing evenly over the layered ingredients. Repeat the layers with the remaining half of the ingredients. Pour the rest of the dressing over the top and spread evenly.
Reserve a few pieces of egg, bacon, peas, or cheese for garnish and arrange them neatly on top. Cover and refrigerate overnight to allow the flavours to develop.

groups.heading: To Serve
steps: Serve cold as a side dish to grilled meats or as a centrepiece salad at a gathering. Do not toss before serving — the layered presentation is part of its charm!

title: Zannie’s Sweet Mustard
headnote: My late aunt Suzanne Klopper (lovingly called Zannie) made this delectable sweet mustard sauce. It’s delicious, and you can eat it with everything. And if you bottle it, you can keep it in the fridge for 6 months… not that it would last that long.

groups.heading: For Zannie’s Sweet Mustard Sauce
steps: Whisk all the ingredients together until smooth.
Cook in a double boiler (or use a glass bowl over a pot of boiling water) for 20-30 minutes until the mixture thickens. Stir occasionally.
Store in the refrigerator once cooled.

title: Marikie’s Koeksisters
headnote: Another Marikie recipe. My cousin’s husband is obsessed with Koeksisters, so my mom gave them this recipe to make koeksisters in London, where they live. We tested this recipe together… and it is a really cool recipe! Traditional South African syrup-drenched plaits — sweet, crisp, and deliciously sticky.

groups.heading: For the syrup
steps: Combine all the syrup ingredients in a saucepan. Bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Once boiling, reduce to medium heat and simmer for 5 minutes without stirring. Remove from heat, strain to remove solids, and transfer to a glass bowl. Refrigerate overnight.

groups.heading: For the dough
ingredients: Vegetable oil, for deep frying (±750 ml)
steps: In a large bowl, sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Rub the butter into the dry ingredients using your fingertips until it resembles breadcrumbs.

In a separate bowl, beat the eggs and milk lightly. Gradually add to the dry ingredients, mixing continuously until a soft, pliable dough forms. Knead on a floured surface until smooth. Cover and let rest for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Roll the rested dough out to about ¼ inch (5 mm) thick on a lightly oiled surface. Cut into strips about 10 cm x 1.5 cm. Twist or braid each strip, pinching the ends to seal.
Heat the oil in a deep fryer or large pot to 180°C. Fry the koeksisters in batches, turning until golden brown (2–3 minutes per side).
Remove with a slotted spoon and immediately dip them into the cold syrup. Coat thoroughly. Let cool on a wire rack.

Best enjoyed once cooled and sticky. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for several days or freeze for longer storage. If frozen, allow to sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Easy Peasy Baklava
headnote: I love a good baklava. And this recipe is so easy and delicious… you’ll make a batch every week.

groups.heading: For the Baklava
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a deep baking tray.
In a food processor, grind the cashews and 40gr of the pistachios with the sugar until rough.
Place a few sheets of phyllo pastry in the baking dish. Brush with some ghee, then layer with nuts. Repeat this twice. Cover with rest of the ground up pistachios.
Cut into three rows, and then diagonally. Bake for 10 minutes. Once removed, let the baklava cool down.

title: No-Bake Fridge Cheesecake
headnote: Our goddaughter, Lua, is a big fan of Cheesecake. This is a really easy no-bake cheesecake that anyone can pull off!

groups.heading: For the Crust
ingredients: 1 packet (200 g) Tennis biscuits, finely crushed
steps: Mix the crushed Tennis biscuits with the melted butter. Press the mixture firmly into the base of a springform (loose-bottom) pan. Refrigerate while you prepare the filling.

groups.heading: For Filling
ingredients: 30 ml cold water (to bloom the gelatine)
30 ml boiling water (to dissolve the gelatine)
250 ml cream (or imitation cream), whipped to stiff peaks
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the Cremora and cold water until smooth. Add the condensed milk and cottage cheese, and whisk until well combined.

Sprinkle the gelatine over 30 ml cold water and let it stand for 10 minutes to bloom. Add 30 ml boiling water and stir until the gelatine is fully dissolved. Stir the gelatine mixture into the Cremora filling.
Stir in the lemon juice until fully incorporated. Gently fold in the whipped cream until smooth and airy.
Pour the filling into the prepared crust. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or until set.
Just before serving, top the cheesecake with lightly mashed fresh raspberries or fruit of your choice.

title: Jan Ellis Pudding
headnote: Jan Ellis Pudding is such a staple in a South African inspired menu. This one works every time!

groups.heading: For the cake
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Spray a heatproof dish with a volume of 2 liters.
Dissolve the bicarbonate of soda in the milk. Mix the rest of the dough ingredients. Stir in the soda-milk mixture and mix very well.
Pour the dough into the prepared dish and bake for 30 minutes.

groups.heading: For the syrup
steps: Meanwhile, combine all the sauce ingredients and bring to a boil.
Pour a little of the warm sauce over the warm pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven. Let the pudding stand for a while so that the sauce can soak in.
Serve lukewarm with thin custard or cream.

title: Apple or Pear Pie
headnote: You can make this with canned apple or pear pieces… it's delicious either way!

groups.heading: For the cake
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a pie dish (23cm).
Cream butter & sugar. Add the eggs and beat until light and fluffy. Sift in flour and salt and fold into the mixture. Add the milk and mix well.
Turn into the greased pie dish. Arrange apple/pear pieces in the pie dish. Mix the cinnamon and sugar and sprinkle over the apple/pear pieces.
Bake for 30 minutes.

groups.heading: For the syrup
steps: Meanwhile, mix the ingredients for the syrup into a small pot on a medium heat until well combined.
Pur the syrup over the pie as it comes out of the oven. Serve either hot or cold with marscopone.

title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
headnote: This is one of my mom’s go-to recipes when she has guests over for coffee.

groups.heading: For the cake
ingredients: 250 g unsalted butter (plus extra for greasing)
Zest of 3 lemons (reserve the juice for the drizzle)
steps: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease a loaf tin and line with baking paper.
Combine all cake ingredients in a large bowl and beat until smooth.
Spoon mixture into the tin, smooth out the top, and bake for 40-50 minutes or until a skewer comes out clean.

groups.heading: For the drizzle
ingredients: Juice of 1.5 lemons (adjust based on size and juiciness)
steps: While the cake is still warm, poke holes all over with a skewer or knife.
Mix icing sugar with lemon juice to form a thin paste. Pour the lemon drizzle over the cake, allowing it to soak in.

title: Ultimate Chocolate Brownies
headnote: This is the ultimate chocolate brownie recipe.

groups.heading: For the cake
steps: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease a 20cm x 20cm baking tray, and line with baking paper.
Beat eggs, sugar, and vanilla essence until smooth. Mix in the butter. Sift in flour, cocoa and salt. Once mixed, add roughly cut chocolate pieces and mix in.
Deposit mixture into the prepped baking tray. Top with generous amount of sea salt flakes.
Bake for 45-55 minutes. The brownie is baked when you place a tooth pick in the brownie and it comes out clean. Turn over on a cooling rack.

groups.heading: For the ganache
steps: Mix the ingredients for the ganache in a small pot over a medium heat until combined.
Pour over the baked brownie and let cool. cut into squares and enjoy!

title: Sunday, Bloody Sunday
headnote: This take on a Bloody Mary is a staple in our house… especially on Sunday’s. We make a big jug that’ll last till lunch!

groups.heading: You’ll need…
ingredients: 1 pt Vodka per serving (100ml for a jug)
2 tsp Tajin (plus extra for the glass rim)
steps: Rim a tall glass with honey and Tajin.
Mix all ingredients in a shaker/food processor with ice.
Strain into a chilled glass and serve with celery stick, pickles and olives.

title: The Mieu-Mieu Mule
headnote: When I feel sorry for myself (which happened a lot during Covid) I usually use the words “mieu-Mieu” to express my utter dislike of the situation. One day during the pandemic I created this little cocktail to help with the bleakness… and it did!

groups.heading: You’ll need…
steps: Rim a tumbler with brown sugar.
Mix all ingredients in a shaker with ice. Strain into a chilled glass and serve with a lime coin.

title: The Vesper
headnote: My favourite version of a Martini, which I love!

groups.heading: You’ll need…
steps: Mix all the ingredients in a shaker with ice. Serve in a Martini glass. Garnish an olive.

title: The Turkish Delight
headnote: My dad’s favourite sweet was a Turkish Delight… and this is a homage to my dad, Louis Botha.

groups.heading: You’ll need…
steps: Mix all the ingredients except for the ginger ale in a shaker with ice. Top it all off with Ginger ale.

caption: A portrait of my late Dad - Louis Botha - which was done by my cousin (twice removed), Christiaan Conradie. www.christiaanconradie.com

title: El Pepino Verde
headnote: This is such a refreshing cocktail. And easy to make…

groups.heading: You’ll need…
steps: Mix the gin, lemon juice and elderflower syrup in a shaker with ice. Pour into a glass and garnish with cucumber ribbon.

title: Lost Boys Liquid
headnote: This is a favourite with our friends Zavion & John Kotze-Brereton. Our WhatsApp group’s name is “The Lost Boys” (from Peter Pan), and we always have these when we see each other.

groups.heading: You’ll need…
steps: Add all ingredients except for the coffee beans in a shaker. Add ice and shake vigoursly for 20 seconds.
Pour through a stainer into a martini glass and garish with coffee beans.

title: Negroni
headnote: A timeless Italian aperitif — bitter, bold, and beautifully balanced. I really like this cocktail… and I might be alone on this island.

groups.heading: You’ll need…
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice to chill while you prepare the drink.
In a mixing glass, add the gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth. Add ice and stir gently for 20–30 seconds until well chilled.
Discard the ice from the serving glass. Strain the cocktail into the glass over fresh ice.
Express the oils from a twist of orange peel over the drink, then drop it in as garnish.

tips: For a smoother sip, try equal parts over a large ice cube, or for a modern twist, swap the gin for mezcal or prosecco (a Negroni Sbagliato).

title: Michelada
headnote: A smoky, spicy Mexican beer cocktail with mezcal and a chilli-lime kick. Perfect for hot days, smoky braais, or spicy food pairings!

groups.heading: You’ll need…
ingredients: 2 tsp Tajin (plus extra for the glass rim)
steps: Rim a tall glass with honey and Tajin.
In a shaker filled with ice, combine the mezcal, lime juice, honey, Tabasco, Balsamic Vinegar, tomato juice, and Worcestershire sauce. Shake briefly to chill.
Strain the mixture into the prepared glass over fresh ice. Top with chilled lager. Garnish with a lime wedge.

tips: Keep the remaining beer nearby to top up as needed.
